newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Changing HK laws may drive out investors -- Tsang.
newsitem.headline: Changing HK laws may drive out investors -- Tsang.

text.p: Hong Kong's Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said Chinese proposals to alter Hong Kong's laws could drive out foreign investors and cause civil unrest.
Tsang told the South China Morning Post newspaper in an interview published on Thursday that investors may pull out if China fails to convince them that making substantive changes is necessary.
A Beijing-controlled panel last Sunday proposed diluting Hong Kong laws on civil liberties and elections, including part of its Bill of Rights, when China takes over five months from now.

"If you can't convince the people of Hong Kong, people may take to the streets, some may keep their frustration in their hearts, some in the civil service may quit. Some may emigrate," the post quoted Tsang as saying.
"Investors are similar. They talk about substance (of the laws). If they are happy with it, they will invest more. If they aren't, they will leave," Tsang was quoted as saying.
But Tsang said political squabbles in the past few years had not had an adverse impact on the economy.
He said investors would continue to invest if they were convinced such fundamentals as the rule of law, a free market, a level playing field and a free press would continue unabated.

He said economic data indicated the Hong Kong economy would begin to pick up this year and pledged his 1997/98 budget -- which straddles the handover -- would contain no sweeping changes to the tax structure of government expenditure.
